keywords.def: a meem with no vowel (a sukoon or no mark)
saying the meem clearly before every other letter

questions.q: Name the rule in «غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍۢ» (95:6): look at the meem in the middle of the second word.
questions.a: Izhar shafawi: meem sakinah before ن inside the word.

questions.q: Three-rule hunt (pupil PDF): label every meem sakinah in Al-Fil 105:1 to 5. Today's rota group recites 95:4 and 5 to the teacher.
questions.a: 105:1 أَلَمْ تَرَ: izhar; 105:2 أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ: izhar; 105:2 كَيْدَهُمْ فِى: izhar; 105:3 عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا: izhar; 105:4 تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍۢ: ikhfa.

questions.q: Extend: which meem rule happens most often in Al-Fil?
questions.a: Izhar shafawi (four times); ikhfa shafawi once.

questions.q: Stretch: explain why we take extra care before ف in «كَيْدَهُمْ فِى» (105:2).
questions.a: ف is near the lips, so the meem could be hidden by mistake; it must be clear.
A) فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ. Meem sakinah before أ: izhar shafawi. The others are ikhfa and idgham.

questions.q: Izhar shafawi means the meem is ...
Think again: Say 'hum-wa' and 'hum-fa' quickly. Why might your lips want to skip the meem?
questions.a: و and ف also use the lips, so the meem can slip. Izhar shafawi means we keep it clear.
